q: 1. The symbol SP indicates .............
explain: In USCS notation, SP denotes poorly graded sand.

q: 2. The expansion of soil due to shear at a constant pressure is called as
explain: Dilatancy is the volumetric expansion that dense granular soils undergo when sheared, as particles ride over one another, even under constant confining pressure.

q: 3. The symbol GM indicates .............
explain: In USCS notation, GM denotes silty gravel.

q: 4. The symbol SC indicates .............
explain: In USCS notation, SC denotes clayey sand.

q: 5. Which of the following clays behave like a dense sand .............
options: over consolidated clay with a low OCR
over consolidated clay with a high OCR
explain: Heavily over-consolidated clay (high OCR) exhibits dilative, brittle behaviour similar to dense sand under shear.

q: 6. In hydrometer analysis, equation is derived based on
explain: Hydrometer analysis (for fine-grained particle-size distribution) uses Stoke's law, which relates the terminal settling velocity of spherical particles in a fluid to their diameter.

q: 7. The ratio of plasticity index to clay fraction is known as .............
explain: Activity of clay is defined as plasticity index divided by the percentage of clay-sized fraction (Skempton's activity).

q: 8. Plasticity needle is used to determine
options: Plastic limit of the soil used in compaction
Penetration resistance to control field compaction
Penetration value of bitumen used in road construction
Swelling index of black cotton soils
explain: The plasticity/proctor needle is a field device used to measure penetration resistance, helping control and verify field compaction quality against the laboratory compaction curve.

q: 9. Bitumen, when added to soil, mainly
explain: Bitumen stabilization primarily works by coating soil particles to reduce water absorption and infiltration, essentially acting as a waterproofing/binding agent.

q: 10. Van Shear test is used for
options: Measuring shear strength of Cohesive soil of low shear strength
Measuring void ratio of sandy soils
explain: The vane shear test is specifically designed to measure the undrained shear strength of soft, saturated cohesive soils with low shear strength, in-situ or in the lab.

q: 11. Thixotropy refers to
options: Flow of highly viscous fluids through soil
Increase in thickness of soil fabric
explain: Thixotropy is the phenomenon where a remoulded clay soil, left undisturbed at constant water content, gradually regains (increases) part of its lost strength over time.

q: 12. Black cotton soil is not suitable for foundations because of its .............
explain: Black cotton soil contains montmorillonite, causing severe volumetric swelling and shrinkage with moisture changes, making it problematic for foundations.

q: 13. China clay is also called .............
explain: China clay is the common name for kaolin, dominated by the kaolinite clay mineral.

q: 14. In the field, Rolling test is used to differentiate clay from .............
explain: The rolling (toughness) test helps distinguish clay's plasticity from the low or non-plastic behaviour of silts.

q: 15. For classification purposes, coarse grained soils shall be divided into following number of sub-divisions .............
explain: Coarse-grained soils are divided into two main sub-divisions: gravels (G) and sands (S).

q: 16. For classification purposes, fine grained soils shall be divided into following number of sub-divisions based on liquid limit .............
explain: Fine-grained soils are divided into three sub-divisions based on liquid limit: low, intermediate, and high compressibility.

q: 17. The coarse grained soils will lie on boundary classification when they have this percentage of fines .............
explain: USCS boundary (dual) classification applies to coarse-grained soils with 5-12% fines content.

q: 18. When the plasticity index of a soil is zero, the soil is
explain: A zero plasticity index means the soil shows no plastic range (liquid limit ≈ plastic limit or cannot be determined), characteristic of non-plastic cohesionless soils like sand.

q: 19. The basis for the classification of the grained soils is .............
explain: Fine-grained soil sub-classification relies on the plasticity chart (relating liquid limit and plasticity index).

q: 20. Relative density of a compacted dense sand is approximately equal to
explain: A well-compacted, dense sand approaches its densest possible state (e close to emin), giving a relative density close to but just under 1.0, i.e., approximately 0.95.

q: 21. The deflocculating agent which is used in the sedimentation analysis is .............
explain: Sodium hexametaphosphate is the standard dispersing/deflocculating agent used to keep particles separated during sedimentation analysis.

q: 22. Hydroscopic water can be removed in the lab. by oven-drying at a temp. of .............
explain: Standard oven drying at 105-110°C is sufficient to remove hygroscopic moisture from soil samples.

q: 23. A pycnometer is used to determine
explain: A pycnometer determines the specific gravity of soil solids directly, and (for soils of known G) can also be used to back-calculate water content.

q: 24. Stoke's law is valid only if the size of particle is
explain: Stoke's law (for laminar settling used in hydrometer analysis) is valid within the particle size range of roughly 0.2 mm down to 0.0002 mm; outside this range turbulence or Brownian motion invalidates it.

q: 25. Textural classification is merely based on .............
explain: Textural classification systems (like USDA) classify soil purely by percentage of sand, silt, and clay sized particles, i.e., grain size.

q: 26. The effective size of the soil is .............
explain: The effective size of a soil is conventionally defined as D10, the sieve size through which 10% of particles pass.

q: 27. Uniformify co-efficient is the ratio of .............
explain: Uniformity coefficient Cu = D60/D10, comparing the 60% and 10% passing sizes.

q: 28. In which type of soil the cohesive force is assumed to be zero
explain: Sandy (granular) soils lack significant inter-particle attraction, so cohesion is taken as zero (c=0) in strength analysis, unlike clayey soils.

q: 29. In the laboratory determination of SL the volume of the dry soil pat is determined by .............
explain: In shrinkage limit determination, the volume of the oven-dried soil pat is measured (often via mercury displacement, but per key here noted under oven dry method).

q: 30. Shrinkage ratio will be equal to .............
explain: Shrinkage ratio numerically equals the mass specific gravity (dry unit weight/unit weight of water), closely related to grain specific gravity in these formulations.

q: 31. The slope of the flow curve obtained in liquid limit test is called .............
explain: The slope of the water content vs. log(number of blows) curve in the liquid limit test defines the flow index.

q: 32. Two soils A and B are having a flow index of 9 and 6 respectively. Then which soil has a better strength as function of WC .............
explain: A lower flow index indicates a steeper strength-loss curve with moisture change, meaning soil B (flow index 6) retains strength better with changing water content.

q: 33. The ratio of plasticity index to flow index is called .............
explain: Toughness index is defined as the ratio of plasticity index to flow index.

q: 34. Specific surface of the following soil is more .............
explain: Clay particles are the smallest and most plate-like, giving them by far the highest specific surface area.

q: 35. More hygroscopicity will be observed in .............
explain: Clay's high specific surface and mineral structure make it absorb the most moisture from the atmosphere (hygroscopicity).

q: 36. If kerosene is used instead of water in the Pycnometer method of determination of grain specific gravity, the expression for the grain specific gravity .............
options: should be added to the sp. gravity of kerosene
should be multiplied by the sp. gravity of kerosene
should be divided by the sp. gravity of kerosene
should be subtracted by the sp. gravity of kerosene
explain: When kerosene replaces water (useful for gypsum/soluble soils), the result must be divided by kerosene's own specific gravity to reference it back to water.

q: 37. The maximum shear stress occurs on the filament which makes an angle with the horizontal plane equal to .............
explain: Maximum shear stress in a Mohr's circle analysis occurs on the plane inclined at 45° to the principal planes.

q: 38. When the consistency index is zero, then the soil s at its .............
explain: Consistency index CI = 0 means natural water content equals the liquid limit, so the soil is at its liquid limit.

q: 39. The unconfined compression test can be conducted on .............
explain: Because it relies on the specimen standing unconfined, the unconfined compression test only works on cohesive (clayey) soils that can self-support.

q: 40. In the pipette analysis, the sampling depth will be .............
explain: In pipette analysis, samples are withdrawn from a fixed, constant depth at different time intervals.

q: 41. The assumption in sedimentation analysis is as follows .............
options: particles settle independent of other particles
walls of the jar where in settlement analysis is done do not affect the settlement
explain: Sedimentation analysis relies on all these idealizing assumptions together: spherical particles, independent settling, and negligible jar-wall effects.

q: 42. A soil is in a semi-solid state, if the consistency index is .............
explain: A consistency index greater than 1 (natural water content below plastic limit) places the soil in the semi-solid to solid state.

q: 43. The liquid limit minus plastic limit is termed as .............
explain: Plasticity index PI = LL - PL, the range of water content over which soil behaves plastically.

q: 44. The correction to be applied to hydrometer reading is .............
explain: All three corrections — meniscus, temperature, and dispersing agent — must be applied to raw hydrometer readings.

q: 45. The composite correction to be applied for in a hydrometer reading is .............
explain: The composite correction combines meniscus, dispersing agent, and temperature corrections in the specific signed combination C = Cm - Cd ± Ct.

q: 46. Hydrometers are usually calibrated at a temperature of .............
explain: Standard soil hydrometers are factory-calibrated at 24°C, requiring correction if the test is run at a different temperature.

q: 47. With the increase of deflocculating agent, the density of soil suspension will .............
explain: Excess dispersing agent adds dissolved solids that lower the relative density reading compared to a plain water blank, requiring correction.

q: 48. Minimum size of the particles of silt soil is
explain: Silt particles range from about 0.002 mm (the upper limit of clay) up to about 0.075 mm, so the minimum size of a silt particle corresponds to 0.002 mm, bordering the clay fraction.

q: 49. Stoke's law is applicable when the effective diameter of the particles is less than .............
explain: Per the reference key, Stoke's Law validity in this context is bounded at particle sizes below about 0.0002 mm.

q: 50. Samples from auger boring are .............
explain: Auger boring mixes and disturbs the soil during extraction, yielding only non-representative (highly disturbed) samples.
